newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Kuo Yang to raise T$7 bln for land plan.
newsitem.headline: Kuo Yang to raise T$7 bln for land plan.

text.p: Taiwan's Kuo Yang Construction said on Thursday it would raise T$7 billion for a land investment project on hopes of a rebound in the property market.
Hug Chiu, a spokesman for Kuo Yang, told Reuters six underwriters, including Grand Cathay Securities, have agreed to provide loans for the fund.
"T$5 billion (of the fund) would be raised through the issuance of company shares starting from May," Chiu said.

Another T$1 billion would be raised through an issue of unsecured company bonds at the end of March, while the remaining T$1 billion would be obtained through the release of convertible bonds in the second half of May, Chiu said.
He said Kuo Yang planned to buy three or four plots of land -- with a total area of about 396,000 square feet -- valued at T$10 billion.
Kuo Yang already had signed a T$4.8 billion deal to buy a lot near the train station in the Sungshan district of Taipei city, Chiu said. But he did not identify the current landowner.
Chiu said his company anticipated a rebound in the property market, which had slumped in the past several years.
Kuo Yang's share price has surged nearly 70 percent over 1997 to stand at T$72.50 at Thursday's close.
On March 7, the Taiwan cabinet's Development Fund announced it would include domestic construction companies under its low-interest T$10 billion loan plan to strengthen competitiveness.
Under the plan, each construction firm can apply for up to T$400 million worth of loans at an annual loan rate of 6.45-6.57 percent.
